meta.cite: Barton O. Oliver's mTOR Atlas. doi:10.5281/zenodo.22059963

data.claim: Resistance exercise / mechanical load activates mTORC1
data.mechanism: Mechanical loading raises mTORC1 signalling in skeletal muscle. Rapamycin given to human volunteers blocks the contraction-induced increase in muscle protein synthesis, placing mTORC1 causally between the load and the response.
data.boundary: Compressed: load reaches mTORC1 through several routes, only some of which need IGF-1, and the map draws one arrow. The human evidence establishes that mTORC1 is required, not which upstream route carries the signal.
